title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for parallel multi-tool calls, injection, and retries
author: Diego Morales
release_notes: - Improve tool-calling execution ergonomics for parallel/multi-tool scenarios; - Add deterministic injection ordering and idempotent retries for tool results; - Streaming stability fixes when injecting tool outputs into active responses
description: Motivation: customers are running multi-tool and parallel tool flows that surface two classes of problems: 1) nondeterministic result injection ordering under parallel tool executions causing confusing assistant responses, and 2) brittle retry semantics that can duplicate or drop tool outputs during streaming responses. This PR implements a conservative, production-friendly execution ergonomics model that ensures deterministic injection ordering, idempotent retries, and improved streaming stability for injected tool outputs. High-level changes: 1) Introduced an execution coordinator that sequences injection points for multi-tool responses by explicit invocation order and declared dependencies rather than arrival time. 2) Added a per-request tool-result ledger that assigns stable injection IDs and de-duplicates replayed results during retries. 3) Implemented a retry/backoff policy that is idempotent by default and integrates with the streaming layer to resume partial chunks without re-emitting already-injected tokens. 4) Exposed opt-in flags on the OpenAI-compat layer to preserve previous behavior for backward compatibility. Commits: ["coord: add execution coordinator for multi-tool sequencing","tools: add per-request result ledger and stable injection ids","streaming: resume streaming without double-emitting injected tokens","api: expose compat flags for legacy injection semantics","tests: add deterministic integration tests for parallel tool calls"]. Files changed (high level): ["pkg/tooling/execution/coordinator.go","pkg/tooling/ledger/ledger.go","pkg/streaming/injector.go","pkg/api/openai_compat.go","internal/tests/tool_call_parallel_test.go","docs/api/tool-calling.md","cmd/runner/entrypoint.go","pkg/runtime/retries.go","pkg/runtime/retries_test.go"]. Tests and CI: CI initially failed on a flaky streaming unit test; I adjusted the test harness timing and added extra integration tests that cover partial-chunk resume and duplicate suppression. All checks passed after one rerun. Review summary: Asha requested clarifications on the ledger lifecycle and GC semantics; I replied explaining that ledgers are ephemeral per request and GC on request completion or 30s inactivity and added comments to ledger.go. Miguel asked for a stronger perf analysis; I added microbenchmarks showing median latency change <3ms for common single-tool paths and a 12% improvement in tail latency for batched parallel tool workloads due to reduced blocking. Ruth requested an opt-out flag for legacy behavior in the compat layer, which I added as openai_compat.LegacyInjectionMode. Backwards compatibility: default is the new safe mode; flag allows teams to opt into legacy ordering. Migration notes: no data migration required; behavior change gated behind request-level flags and runtime config for Dedicated customers. Rollout: feature-gated behind runtime flag and rollout scheduled to Canary for 48 hours, then region-wide. Monitoring: added metrics tool_injection.dedup_events, tool_injection.retry_count, tool_injection.injection_latency_p50/p95. Known limitations: complex cyclic tool dependency graphs still require explicit dependency hints; coordinator currently enforces a conservative linearization. Merge: squash and merge.
